```{ojs}
u5oQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0e7490 0%,#1d4ed8 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(29,78,216,.4);">
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(29,78,216,.12);color:#1d4ed8;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="3000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.className = "u5o-opt";
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;";
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        const opts = card.querySelectorAll("button.u5o-opt");
        opts.forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          opts[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          opts[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    fb.className = "u5o-fb";
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Anchor Phenomenon: Are Storms Getting Worse? {#anchor-phenomenon}

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌀 It has felt like storms are getting worse

<div style="font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; margin: 18px 0;">
It felt like hurricanes and blizzards were really bad these past few years. What does the data show? Will this continue?
</div>

- In this unit you'll look at **two recent winter storm seasons** (2018–19 and 2019–20) and **two recent Atlantic hurricane seasons** (2018 and 2020).
- You'll look for **patterns**: how many storms, how strong, how long they lasted, where they formed and where they went.
- Then you'll start building an argument: as global temperatures keep rising (remember [Unit 4](../unit4-climate-change/unit4-past-and-future.qmd)), will storms become **more frequent** (happen more often) or **more intense** (stronger)?
:::

**Think about it** before you start:

- What do hurricanes and blizzards have in **common**? How are they **different**?
- Have you lived through a big storm in NYC? What happened?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💬 Ideas classmates often share (try your own first!)

- A **hurricane** has heavy rain and extremely strong wind. A **blizzard** has heavy snow and very strong wind.
- Both can cause a lot of disruption, damage to property, and harm to people.
- Both only happen during **certain months** of the year, and they tend to form and travel in **specific places** on Earth.
- To predict the future, we need to know **what causes** these storms, the **past and current patterns** in how often and how strong they are, and **where and when** they travel.

You'll test each of these ideas in the lessons ahead.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Saved details for both Tell the Story sections. Kept in localStorage when it is available.
u5oDetails = {
  const KEY = "u5o-tell-the-story-v1";
  let state = {details: [], story: {b: "", t: ""}};
  try {
    const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY));
    if (saved && Array.isArray(saved.details)) state = {details: saved.details, story: Object.assign({b: "", t: ""}, saved.story || {})};
  } catch (e) {}
  const subs = [];
  const persist = () => { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state)); } catch (e) {} };
  const notify = () => {
    persist();
    for (let i = subs.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const s = subs[i];
      if (s.el.isConnected) s.seen = true;
      else if (s.seen) { subs.splice(i, 1); continue; }
      s.fn();
    }
  };
  return {
    has: id => state.details.some(d => d.id === id),
    list: () => state.details.slice(),
    toggle: d => {
      state.details = state.details.some(x => x.id === d.id) ? state.details.filter(x => x.id !== d.id) : [...state.details, d];
      notify();
    },
    remove: id => { state.details = state.details.filter(x => x.id !== id); notify(); },
    story: g => state.story[g] || "",
    setStory: (g, t) => { state.story[g] = t; persist(); },
    clear: g => { state.details = state.details.filter(d => d.group !== g); state.story[g] = ""; notify(); },
    subscribe: (el, fn) => subs.push({el, fn, seen: false})
  };
}
```

```{ojs}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// A card of detail rows, each with a save star. items: [{id, detail, html?}]
u5oDetailRows = (title, items, group, label, color) => {
  const box = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-left:8px solid ${color};border-radius:12px;padding:14px 18px;margin:10px 0 4px;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1);">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:800;margin-bottom:4px;color:#1a1a1a;"></div>
  </div>`;
  box.firstElementChild.textContent = title;
  for (const it of items) {
    const row = html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px 12px;align-items:center;padding:10px 0;border-top:1px solid #eee;">
      <div style="flex:1 1 220px;color:#1a1a1a;"></div>
    </div>`;
    if (it.html) row.firstElementChild.innerHTML = it.html; else row.firstElementChild.textContent = it.detail;
    row.appendChild(u5oStar({id: it.id, group, label, detail: it.detail}));
    box.appendChild(row);
  }
  return box;
}
```

```{ojs}
u5oNoticeChips = (group, prefix, sets, color) => {
  const box = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-radius:12px;padding:14px 18px;margin:10px 0 4px;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1);"></div>`;

    for (const c of s.chips) {
      const d = {id: `${prefix}-${s.key}-${c}`, group, label: `Video (${s.short})`, detail: c};
      const b = document.createElement("button");
      b.type = "button";
      const paint = () => {
        const on = u5oDetails.has(d.id);

        b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on);
        b.style.cssText = `min-height:40px;padding:6px 14px;border-radius:50px;border:2px solid ${color};background:${on ? color : "#fff"};color:${on ? "#fff" : "#1e1b4b"};font-weight:700;font-size:.9em;cursor:pointer;`;
      };
      b.onclick = () => u5oDetails.toggle(d);
      u5oDetails.subscribe(b, paint);
      paint();
      row.appendChild(b);
    }
    box.appendChild(h); box.appendChild(row);
  }
  box.appendChild(html`<div style="font-size:.88em;color:#555;">Tap what you noticed. Add anything else in your own words in the Detail Tracker.</div>`);
  return box;
}
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## ❄️ What makes a winter storm a **blizzard**?

The U.S. National Weather Service calls a storm a **blizzard** when, for at least **3 hours**, there are **sustained winds or frequent gusts of 35 mph or more** and **falling or blowing snow** that cuts visibility to **less than ¼ mile**. A blizzard is about **wind and visibility**, not just the amount of snow.
:::

## 📊 Winter Storm Season Graphs {#blizzard-graphs}

These graphs show every **named winter storm** in each season. **The length of each bar shows how long the storm lasted.** The color shows the storm's **category**, based on its snowfall total in "points" (pts = inches of snow).

Pick a season, or compare them. Hover over or tap a bar to read it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 About these graphs

- The storm **names** (Avery, Bruce, ...) come from **The Weather Channel**, which names big winter storms. The National Weather Service does not officially name winter storms.
- The **categories** use the graph's own point scale: more inches of snow means more points and a higher category. This is **not** the same as the hurricane category scale.
- Dates on this page were measured from the PTO graph image, so they are about ±1 day.
:::

```{ojs}
    }
```
```{ojs}
  };
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 One way to tell the blizzard story

1. Both seasons had **many named winter storms** (24 in 2018–19, 19 in 2019–20), so the **number of storms did not go up**.
2. But 2019–20 **started earlier** (October) and had the **most intense storm** of both seasons: Ezekiel, a Category 5 that lasted about 8 days over Thanksgiving.
3. Storms travel **west to east** across the US, and many end in the **Northeast**, near NYC.
4. The heaviest snow falls in the **northern** US: the northern Rockies, upper Midwest and Northeast.
5. **Why it matters:** winter storms bring heavy snow, strong winds and ice that cause deaths, crashes, power outages and closures. If storms change as Earth warms, NYC needs to be ready.

Two seasons are **not enough to show a long-term trend**. That's why you'll look at many decades of storm data in the [Blizzards](unit5-blizzards.qmd) lesson.
:::

## 🗺️ Atlantic Tropical Storm Track Maps: 2018 and 2020 {#tropical-maps}

Your PTO shows the National Weather Service's **North Atlantic Hurricane Tracking Charts**. This map draws the same storms from NOAA's official best-track record (**HURDAT2**). Each line is one storm's path; the **color shows how strong it was** at that point. **Hint from your PTO: the storms start from the lower latitudes (the south!).** A dot marks where each storm started.

Choose a year and a filter, then pick a storm to highlight it. Hover over or tap the map to read the storm at that point.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// NOAA NHC HURDAT2 best tracks (hurdat2-1851-2025), named storms only, positions every 12 hours.

u5oSS = kt => kt >= 137 ? 5 : kt >= 113 ? 4 : kt >= 96 ? 3 : kt >= 83 ? 2 : kt >= 64 ? 1 : 0
u5oCls = (code, kt) => code === "H" ? (kt >= 96 ? "Major hurricane (Cat 3–5)" : "Hurricane (Cat 1–2)") : code === "T" || code === "S" ? "Tropical storm" : code === "D" ? "Tropical depression" : "Extratropical / remnant low"
u5oClsDomain = ["Major hurricane (Cat 3–5)", "Hurricane (Cat 1–2)", "Tropical storm", "Tropical depression", "Extratropical / remnant low"]
u5oClsRange = ["#e879f9", "#ef4444", "#facc15", "#4ade80", "#94a3b8"]
u5oTypeLabel = ({TS: "Tropical storm", H: "Hurricane", MH: "Major hurricane"})
u5oMonths = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"]
u5oDay = s => `${u5oMonths[+s.slice(4, 6) - 1]} ${+s.slice(6, 8)}`
u5oStorms = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(u5oHur).map(([yr, list]) => [yr, list.map(s => ({...s, yr,
  pts: s.trk.map(([lon, lat, kt, code, t]) => ({name: s.name, lon, lat, kt, mph: Math.round(kt * 1.15078 / 5) * 5, cls: u5oCls(code, kt), when: `${u5oMonths[+t.slice(0, 2) - 1]} ${+t.slice(2, 4)}, ${t.slice(4)}:00 UTC`}))
}))]))
u5oTcState = ({yr: "2018", filter: "all", storm: ""})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u5oWorld = {
  const topojson = await require("topojson-client@3.1.0");
  try {
    const t = await d3.json("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/land-50m.json");
    return topojson.feature(t, t.objects.land);
  } catch (e) {
    try {
      const t = await d3.json("../world-110m.json");
      const key = t.objects.land ? "land" : Object.keys(t.objects)[0];
      return topojson.feature(t, t.objects[key]);
    } catch (e2) {
      const t = await d3.json("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/land-110m.json");
      return topojson.feature(t, t.objects.land);
    }
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof u5oTc = {
  const st = u5oTcState;
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.value = {...st};
  const yrRow = document.createElement("div"), fRow = document.createElement("div"), selRow = document.createElement("div");
  yrRow.style.cssText = fRow.style.cssText = "display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;margin:6px 0;";
  selRow.style.cssText = "margin:8px 0 4px;";
  const filters = [["all", "All named storms"], ["hur", "Hurricanes only"], ["major", "Major hurricanes only"], ["us", "Made US landfall"]];
  const pass = s => st.filter === "all" || (st.filter === "hur" && s.type !== "TS") || (st.filter === "major" && s.type === "MH") || (st.filter === "us" && s.us);
  const fire = () => { wrap.value = {...st}; draw(); wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); };
  const draw = () => {
    yrRow.replaceChildren(...["2018", "2020"].map(y => u5oChip(y + " season", st.yr === y, "#c2410c", () => { st.yr = y; st.storm = ""; fire(); })));
    fRow.replaceChildren(...filters.map(([id, label]) => u5oChip(label, st.filter === id, "#9f1239", () => { st.filter = id; st.storm = ""; fire(); })));
    const sel = document.createElement("select");
    sel.setAttribute("aria-label", "Highlight a storm");
    sel.style.cssText = "font-family:inherit;font-size:1em;min-height:42px;padding:6px 10px;border:2px solid #c2410c;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;max-width:100%;";
    const list = u5oStorms[st.yr].filter(pass);
    sel.appendChild(new Option(`🔍 Highlight a storm (${list.length} shown)`, ""));
    for (const s of list) sel.appendChild(new Option(`${s.name} (${u5oTypeLabel[s.type]}${s.cat ? ", Cat " + s.cat : ""})`, s.name));
    sel.value = st.storm;
    sel.onchange = () => { st.storm = sel.value; fire(); };
    selRow.replaceChildren(sel);
  };
  draw();
  wrap.append(yrRow, fRow, selRow);
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const shown = u5oTcShown;
  const sel = shown.find(s => s.name === u5oTc.storm);
  const pts = shown.flatMap(s => s.pts);
  const selPts = sel ? sel.pts : [];
  const starts = shown.map(s => s.pts[0]);
  const w = Math.max(300, width);
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: w,
    projection: {type: "mercator", domain: {type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: [[-105, 6], [5, 6], [-105, 60], [5, 60]]}},
    style: {background: "#0b2545", color: "#e2e8f0"},
    color: {domain: u5oClsDomain, range: u5oClsRange},
    marks: [
      Plot.graticule({stroke: "#ffffff", strokeOpacity: 0.12}),
      Plot.geo(u5oWorld, {fill: "#3f5872", stroke: "#8aa0b8", strokeWidth: 0.5}),
      Plot.line(pts, {x: "lon", y: "lat", z: "name", stroke: "cls", strokeWidth: sel ? 1.2 : (w < 500 ? 1.6 : 2.2), strokeOpacity: sel ? 0.3 : 0.95, curve: "catmull-rom"}),
      Plot.dot(starts, {x: "lon", y: "lat", r: sel ? 2 : 3, fill: "#ffffff", fillOpacity: sel ? 0.4 : 0.9}),
      sel ? Plot.line(selPts, {x: "lon", y: "lat", stroke: "cls", strokeWidth: 5, curve: "catmull-rom"}) : null,
      sel ? Plot.dot([selPts[0]], {x: "lon", y: "lat", r: 6, fill: "#ffffff", stroke: "#0b2545", strokeWidth: 2}) : null,
      sel ? Plot.text([selPts[0]], {x: "lon", y: "lat", text: () => `${sel.name} starts here`, dy: 14, fill: "#ffffff", fontWeight: 800, fontSize: 13, stroke: "#0b2545", strokeWidth: 3}) : null,
      Plot.tip(sel ? selPts : pts, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat", maxRadius: 24,
        title: d => `${d.name} · ${d.when}\n${d.cls}\nWinds about ${d.mph} mph`}))
    ]
  });
  const fig = html`<div style="margin:6px 0;"></div>`;
  fig.appendChild(html`<div style="font-weight:800;font-size:1.1em;">${u5oTc.yr} North Atlantic tropical storm tracks</div>`);
  fig.appendChild(html`<div style="font-size:.9em;opacity:.85;margin-bottom:6px;">${shown.length} storm${shown.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} shown · source: NOAA National Hurricane Center HURDAT2</div>`);
  fig.appendChild(Plot.legend({color: {domain: u5oClsDomain, range: u5oClsRange}, swatchSize: 14, style: {fontSize: "12px", color: "inherit", background: "transparent"}}));
  const box = html`<div style="border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;"></div>`;
  box.appendChild(chart);
  fig.appendChild(box);
  return fig;
}
```

```{ojs}
      <b>${u5oTc.yr} at a glance:</b> ${list.length} named storms · ${list.filter(x => x.type !== "TS").length} hurricanes · ${list.filter(x => x.type === "MH").length} major hurricanes · first named storm ${list[0].name} (${u5oDay(list[0].named)}) · last ${list[list.length - 1].name} (${u5oDay(list[list.length - 1].named)}).<br>
      <b>${us.length} made landfall on the US mainland:</b> ${us.join(", ")}.<br>
      <span style="color:#555;">Pick a storm above to see its details.</span></div>`;
  }
  const card = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1a1a1a;border-left:8px solid ${s.type === "MH" ? "#c026d3" : s.type === "H" ? "#dc2626" : "#ca8a04"};border-radius:12px;padding:14px 18px;margin:10px 0 4px;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1);">
    <div style="font-size:1.15em;font-weight:800;color:#1a1a1a;">${u5oTypeLabel[s.type]} ${s.name} (${s.yr})</div>
    <div style="margin:6px 0;font-size:.95em;color:#1a1a1a;">
      📅 ${u5oDay(s.start)} – ${u5oDay(s.end)} · 💨 Peak winds about <b>${s.mph} mph</b>${s.cat ? ` (<b>Category ${s.cat}</b>)` : ""} · 🔻 Lowest pressure ${s.minp} mb · ${s.us ? "🇺🇸 Made US landfall" : "Did not make US mainland landfall"}
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const detail = `${s.yr}: ${u5oTypeLabel[s.type]} ${s.name} lasted ${u5oDay(s.start)} – ${u5oDay(s.end)}, peak winds about ${s.mph} mph${s.cat ? " (Category " + s.cat + ")" : ""}${s.us ? ", and made US landfall" : ""}.`;
  const row = html`<div style="display:flex;justify-content:flex-end;"></div>`;
  row.appendChild(u5oStar({id: `t-m-storm-${s.yr}-${s.name}`, group: "t", label: "Maps", detail}));
  card.appendChild(row);
  return card;
}
```

```{ojs}
  }
])
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 Why do the PTO graph and NOAA's final records differ for 2020?

After every season, the National Hurricane Center re-checks all its data and writes a final report on each storm. For 2020, two storms were **upgraded** after the season:

- **Gamma** was upgraded from a tropical storm to a **Category 1 hurricane**.
- **Zeta** was upgraded from Category 2 to a **Category 3 (major) hurricane** at its Louisiana landfall.

So NOAA's final count for 2020 is **30 named storms, 14 hurricanes and 7 major hurricanes**. The PTO graph shows the earlier counts (30 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 6 major). For 2018, both agree: **15 named storms, 8 hurricanes, 2 major hurricanes** (Florence and Michael).

The PTO graphs count only **named** storms, so the depression and subtropical columns are 0. (There were also a few weaker depressions that never got names.)
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{

  const data = ["2018", "2020"].flatMap(yr => u5oStorms[yr].map(s => ({yr, name: s.name, ...doy(s.named)})).sort((a, b) => a.d - b.d).map((d, i) => ({...d, n: i + 1})));
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: Math.max(300, width),

    marginLeft: 40, marginRight: 20,
    x: {type: "utc", domain: [new Date(Date.UTC(2000, 4, 1)), new Date(Date.UTC(2000, 11, 1))], tickFormat: d3.utcFormat("%b"), label: null, grid: true},
    y: {label: "↑ Named storms so far", domain: [0, 31], grid: true},

      Plot.text([{x: new Date(Date.UTC(2000, 5, 4)), y: 29}], {x: "x", y: "y", text: () => "Official season: June 1 – Nov 30", textAnchor: "start", fill: "currentColor", fontSize: 11}),
      Plot.line(data, {x: "d", y: "n", stroke: "yr", curve: "step-after", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot(data, {x: "d", y: "n", fill: "yr", r: 3}),
      Plot.tip(data, Plot.pointer({x: "d", y: "n", title: d => `${d.yr}: #${d.n} ${d.name}, named ${d3.utcFormat("%b %-d")(d.d)}`}))
    ]
  });
  const fig = html`<div style="margin:16px 0 6px;"><div style="font-weight:800;font-size:1.1em;">How fast did the names pile up?</div>
    <div style="font-size:.9em;opacity:.85;margin-bottom:4px;">Each step is a new named storm (date it reached tropical-storm strength). Source: NOAA HURDAT2.</div></div>`;
  fig.appendChild(chart);
  return fig;
}
```

## Overall Story: Tropical Storm Seasons {#tropical-story}

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: What is the overall story of the 2018 and 2020 US tropical storm seasons? (p. 7)

- Under the graphs, jot **2–3 observations** that tell the story of recent tropical storm seasons.
- Take turns sharing; decide which **3–5 observations** are most important to the story, and **why it matters**.
:::

### ⭐ Detail Tracker: Tropical Storms

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u5oTracker("t")
```

::: {.key-idea .tropical}
### 💡 One way to tell the tropical storm story

1. 2020 had **twice as many named storms** as 2018 (30 vs. 15), a record, and so many that it ran out of names.
2. 2020 also had **more hurricanes** (14 vs. 8) and **more than three times as many major hurricanes** (7 vs. 2).
3. Storms **start in the warm tropics** (the south), move west, then curve north and northeast.
4. Many more storms **hit the US** in 2020 (11 vs. 4), especially the Gulf Coast.
5. **Why it matters:** hurricanes like Maria bring extreme winds, rain and flooding that destroy homes, knock out power for months and kill people.
:::

::: {.mind-blown}
Putting both stories together (from your teacher's guide): over these two years, there were **more tropical storms and hurricanes**, but there was **not an increase in the number of winter storms**. The winter season did bring the **single most intense** winter storm, though. Is this the start of a trend, or just two unusual years?
:::

# Introduction to the Performance Task and Initial Ideas {#performance-task}

::: {.explain-box}
## 🎯 Will there be more frequent and more intense severe storms in the future?

In this unit, your task will be to **write an argument** about how storms will change in **frequency** and **intensity** as global temperatures continue to rise.
:::

| Word | Means | Example from this page |
|---|---|---|
| **Frequency** | How **often** something happens | 15 named storms in 2018 vs. 30 in 2020 |
| **Intensity** | How **strong** a storm is (wind speed, snowfall, pressure) | Ezekiel was Category 5 (more than 100 pts); Michael had 160 mph winds |
| **Prediction** | What you think **will** happen, based on evidence | "I predict more major hurricanes because..." |
| **Explanation** | **Why or how** something happens, using science ideas | "Hurricanes get their energy from warm ocean water, so..." |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🤔 Predictions, explanations and arguments

- An **explanation** tells *how or why* something happens (like how a hurricane forms).
- A **prediction** says what *will* happen. A good scientific prediction is built on an explanation: if you know *why* storms form, you can predict what happens when conditions change.
- An **argument** makes a **claim** (your prediction) and backs it up with **evidence** and **reasoning**. It also takes on a **counterclaim**: evidence that points the other way. Your final task is an argument.
:::

### 💭 Initial Ideas: your predictions

**Individually brainstorm ideas and predictions** for each prompt. There are no wrong answers yet. What matters is what you are **basing your prediction on**. Your answers save in this browser so you can come back and see how your thinking changes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u5oPredictions = {
  const KEY = "u5o-predictions-v1";
  const prompts = [
    {id: "hf", q: "Will hurricanes happen more often in the future?", icon: "🌀", opts: ["Yes, more often", "About the same", "No, less often", "Not sure yet"]},
    {id: "hi", q: "Will hurricanes be more intense in the future?", icon: "🌀", opts: ["Yes, more intense", "About the same", "No, less intense", "Not sure yet"]},
    {id: "bf", q: "Will blizzards happen more often in the future?", icon: "🌨️", opts: ["Yes, more often", "About the same", "No, less often", "Not sure yet"]},
    {id: "bi", q: "Will blizzards be more intense in the future?", icon: "🌨️", opts: ["Yes, more intense", "About the same", "No, less intense", "Not sure yet"]}
  ];
  const bases = ["2018 vs 2020 hurricane data", "2018–19 vs 2019–20 winter storm data", "Warmer air and oceans (Unit 4)", "The news or social media", "My own experience in NYC"];
  let state = {};
  try { state = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)) || {}; } catch (e) {}
  const save = () => { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state)); } catch (e) {} };
  const wrap = html`<div style="margin:10px 0;"></div>`;
  for (const p of prompts) {
    const s = state[p.id] = Object.assign({pick: "", bases: [], why: ""}, state[p.id] || {});
    const card = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:14px 16px;margin-bottom:12px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.1);border-left:6px solid ${p.icon === "🌀" ? "#c2410c" : "#0e7490"};">
      <div style="font-weight:800;margin-bottom:8px;color:#1e1b4b;">${p.icon} ${p.q}</div>
      <div class="opts" style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;"></div>
      <div style="font-weight:700;font-size:.92em;margin:10px 0 6px;color:#1e1b4b;">I'm basing this on:</div>
      <div class="bases" style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;"></div>
      <textarea rows="2" placeholder="Because…" style="font-family:inherit;width:100%;box-sizing:border-box;margin-top:8px;padding:8px;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;font-size:.95em;color:#1e1b4b;background:#fff;"></textarea>
    </div>`;
    const color = p.icon === "🌀" ? "#c2410c" : "#0e7490";
    const opts = card.querySelector(".opts"), bs = card.querySelector(".bases"), ta = card.querySelector("textarea");
    ta.setAttribute("aria-label", "My reasoning: " + p.q);
    const paint = () => {
      opts.replaceChildren(...p.opts.map(o => u5oChip(o, s.pick === o, color, () => { s.pick = s.pick === o ? "" : o; save(); paint(); })));
      bs.replaceChildren(...bases.map(b => {
        const on = s.bases.includes(b);
        const c = u5oChip(b, on, "#64748b", () => { s.bases = on ? s.bases.filter(x => x !== b) : [...s.bases, b]; save(); paint(); });
        c.style.fontSize = ".82em"; c.style.minHeight = "36px";
        return c;
      }));
    };
    ta.value = s.why;
    ta.oninput = () => { s.why = ta.value; save(); };
    paint();
    wrap.appendChild(card);
  }
  const bar = html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;align-items:center;">
    <button type="button" style="min-height:42px;padding:6px 18px;border:none;border-radius:50px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0e7490,#c2410c);color:#fff;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">📋 Copy my predictions</button>
    <span style="font-size:.9em;"></span></div>`;
  const msg = bar.querySelector("span");
  bar.querySelector("button").onclick = async () => {
    const text = "My initial predictions (Unit 5)\n\n" + prompts.map(p => {
      const s = state[p.id];
      return `${p.q}\n- Prediction: ${s.pick || "(not chosen yet)"}\n- Based on: ${s.bases.join("; ") || "(none chosen)"}\n- Because: ${s.why.trim() || "(not written yet)"}`;
    }).join("\n\n");
    try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); msg.textContent = "✅ Copied! Paste it into your packet or notes."; }
    catch (e) {
      const tmp = document.createElement("textarea");
      tmp.value = text; document.body.appendChild(tmp); tmp.select();
      let ok = false;
      try { ok = document.execCommand("copy"); } catch (e2) {}
      tmp.remove();
      msg.textContent = ok ? "✅ Copied!" : "⚠️ Couldn't copy here. Copy your predictions into your packet by hand.";
    }
  };
  wrap.appendChild(bar);
  return wrap;
}
```

### Revisiting the Performance Task {#revisiting-the-performance-task}

After each lesson, you'll return to your PTO and use that lesson's evidence. Each "Connect to the Performance Task" page has the same three parts: **(1)** name the independent and dependent variables, **(2)** gather evidence in a table and build a model of how energy and matter flow in the storm, **(3)** write an argument with a claim **and** a counterclaim.

| After this lesson | Your PTO prompt asks... |
|---|---|
| [Blizzards](unit5-blizzards.qmd) (pp. 9–14) | Choose: will the **frequency** (Task 1) or **intensity** (Task 2) of winter storms where you live increase, decrease, or stay the same as global temperatures increase? |
| [Paths of Severe Storms](unit5-storm-paths.qmd) (pp. 15–16) | Will the **frequency** of winter storms per year where you live increase, decrease, or stay the same as global temperatures increase? |
| [Hurricanes](unit5-hurricanes.qmd) (pp. 17–22) | Choose: will the **frequency** (Task 1) or **intensity** (Task 2) of hurricanes where you live increase, decrease, or stay the same as global temperatures increase? |

```{=html}
    {text: "The 2020 Atlantic hurricane season had more named storms than any season on record.", type: "Fact",
     explanation: "2020 had 30 named storms, beating the old record of 28 set in 2005. It used up the regular name list and needed nine Greek letters."},
    {text: "A blizzard is any storm that drops a lot of snow.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "The National Weather Service defines a blizzard by wind and visibility: winds or frequent gusts of 35 mph or more with snow that cuts visibility below 1/4 mile for at least 3 hours. A heavy, calm snowfall is not a blizzard."},
    {text: "Atlantic hurricanes and tropical storms usually start near the equator's warm waters (low latitudes) and move away from it.", type: "Fact",
     explanation: "On the track maps, almost every storm starts between about 10° and 25° N over warm tropical water, then moves west and curves north."},
    {text: "Atlantic hurricane season only happens in August.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "The official season runs June 1 to November 30. Both 2018 and 2020 even had named storms in May, and 2020's last storm (Iota) formed in mid-November."},
    {text: "Two seasons of storm data are enough to prove that storms are getting worse every year.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "Storm seasons vary a lot from year to year. To find a trend, scientists use many decades of records plus climate models. Two seasons are a starting point for questions."},
    {text: "A hurricane's category (1–5) is based on its maximum sustained wind speed.", type: "Fact",
     explanation: "That's the Saffir-Simpson scale. Category 3 and up (111 mph or more) are 'major' hurricanes. The winter storm graphs in your PTO use a different scale, based on snowfall."},
    {text: "Most winter storms in the US travel from east to west.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "The PTO maps show tracks running west to east, often ending in the Northeast. You'll find out why (global winds) in Paths of Severe Storms."},
    {text: "Hurricane Maria hit Puerto Rico as a weak tropical storm.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017 as a strong Category 4 hurricane with winds near 155 mph, knocking out power to the whole island."}
  ];
  var idx = 0, score = 0, answered = 0, cardAnswered = false;
  function el(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function updateCard() {
    if (idx >= cards.length) {
      el('u5omf-card').style.display = 'none';
      el('u5omf-myth').style.display = 'none';
      el('u5omf-fact').style.display = 'none';
      el('u5omf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
      el('u5omf-next').style.display = 'none';
      el('u5omf-done').style.display = 'block';
      el('u5omf-final').textContent = score;
      el('u5omf-count').textContent = cards.length;
      return;
    }
    el('u5omf-card').textContent = cards[idx].text;
    el('u5omf-progress').textContent = 'Card ' + (idx + 1) + ' of ' + cards.length;
    el('u5omf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
    el('u5omf-next').style.display = 'none';
    el('u5omf-myth').disabled = false;
    el('u5omf-fact').disabled = false;
    el('u5omf-myth').style.opacity = '1';
    el('u5omf-fact').style.opacity = '1';
    cardAnswered = false;
  }
  window.u5omfAnswer = function(choice) {
    if (cardAnswered) return;
    cardAnswered = true;
    answered++;
    var card = cards[idx];
    var correct = (choice === card.type);
    if (correct) score++;
    el('u5omf-score').textContent = score;
    el('u5omf-total').textContent = answered;
    var fb = el('u5omf-feedback');
    fb.style.display = 'block';
    fb.style.background = correct ? 'rgba(0,184,148,0.25)' : 'rgba(214,48,49,0.25)';
    fb.style.border = '1px solid ' + (correct ? '#00b894' : '#e17055');
    fb.innerHTML = '<strong>' + (correct ? '✅ Correct! ' : '❌ That\'s a ' + card.type + '! ') + '</strong>' + card.explanation;
    el('u5omf-myth').disabled = true;
    el('u5omf-fact').disabled = true;
    el('u5omf-myth').style.opacity = (choice === 'Myth') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('u5omf-fact').style.opacity = (choice === 'Fact') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('u5omf-next').style.display = 'block';
  };
  window.u5omfNext = function() { idx++; updateCard(); };
  window.u5omfRestart = function() {
    idx = 0; score = 0; answered = 0;
    el('u5omf-card').style.display = 'flex';
    el('u5omf-myth').style.display = 'block';
    el('u5omf-fact').style.display = 'block';
    el('u5omf-done').style.display = 'none';
    el('u5omf-score').textContent = '0';
    el('u5omf-total').textContent = '0';
    updateCard();
  };
  updateCard();
})();
</script>
```
